synoptic.summary: A deepening, negatively tilted trough moving in from California brings widespread valley rain/snow and mountain snow on Tuesday: rain reaches Salt Lake airport around 08:00 and precipitation chances at the launches climb from 70% (08:00–10:00) to 95–100% from 11:00 through the evening, with surface flow from 150°–190° at 10–22 kt gusting to 33 kt. Tuesday evening the surface flow turns to ~300° behind the front (airport forecast 300°/10 kt G24 from 20:00) with possible snow to the valley floors. Transient ridging gives a dry, cold Wednesday with flow from 150°–170° at 6–13 kt all day — no afternoon switch to 320°–360° is forecast, which departs from the usual diurnal pattern. A broader, longer-lasting storm arrives Thursday with precipitation chances of 83–90% all day. Thunder chances stay low (0–8%). Winds-aloft data failed to download this run, so rotor and mixing-down checks rely on the NWS transport wind and the airport forecasts.
synoptic.afd_excerpt: A trough is deepening and moving into central California which will bring widespread precipitation to most of the CWA tomorrow. This storm will quickly exit Tuesday night with drier conditions for Wednesday. Another more long lasting storm is slated to arrive on Thursday with more widespread precipitation.

pressure.significance: Sea-level pressure at Salt Lake airport (KSLC) fell from 1019.4 mb at 23:54 Sunday to 1011.5 mb at 16:54 Monday and has held near 1012.6–1012.8 mb since — the trough is close; expect a brief rise behind Tuesday's front, then a fall again ahead of Thursday's storm.

observations.summary: Monday-evening observations (18:15–19:45 local), all under 3 h old at fetch time. The south-valley stations show steady flow from 150°–165°: Spanish Fork 157°/14 kt G17 (gusts to 19 kt since), Alpine 153°/9 kt G15, Lehi 164°/9 kt G13 — with the valley-to-launch correction (+3–8 kt) that is already 17–22 kt at launch height, in line with the strong forecast for Tuesday morning. Salt Lake airport has gone light (160°/3 kt), South Valley Regional last reported 340°/11 kt at 18:15. Point of the Mountain and Draper returned no data; Provo returned no wind values. These are evening readings — they confirm the flow from 150°–165° but say little about wind speed at sunrise.
